$ORGO (G85CQ…uBLV) is the Believe-launched token of a real startup, Orgo / Organic Intelligence Inc. (orgo.ai, Berkeley CA; founders Spencer Kinney @spncrk and Nick Vasilescu), which sells sub-second-boot cloud Linux/Windows desktops for computer-use AI agents (its docs explicitly cover Claude Computer Use, OpenAI CUA and OpenClaw). The token launched 2025-07-21 via Believe, was listed on CoinGecko at ~$8.3M mcap in July 2025, hit ATH $0.01718 on 2026-01-31, then decayed for ~8 months to ~$50–60k mcap.

Today (2026-09-22) it printed an ALL-TIME LOW of ~$0.0000922 and then squeezed roughly 8–10x inside a single hour to a 24h high of ~$0.00096, before retracing hard (packet: m5 −24%, m15 −46%; CoinGecko showed $0.00049 and CoinMarketCap $0.00062 minutes apart). Essentially all 24h activity sits inside that one hour: h1 volume $165.8k vs h24 $167.0k; h1 txns 655/362 vs h24 667/368; only 238 unique buyers and 150 unique sellers. That is a thin, compressed, single-burst squeeze on $62.7k of liquidity (~2.6x liquidity turnover in 60 minutes), not broad accumulation.

The most plausible catalyst I can evidence is macro-narrative, not project-specific: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5 today, marketed as its leading model for "agentic coding, computer use and professional knowledge work" at 40% lower cost. ORGO is the most literal "computer-use infrastructure" ticker on Solana, so a rotation bid into that narrative from a dead $50k float would produce exactly this chart. I could NOT find a single tweet, call, Reddit thread or article actually linking today's ORGO move to Opus 5.5 — the link is inference, not evidence.

Corroborating that the ticker is trending right now: three zero-liquidity copycat ORGO tokens were minted at ~18:58–18:59 UTC today (minutes before detection), one literally named "ycomb gives them 500k btw" — sniper bots piling onto a trending name plus a community meme claiming Orgo got Y Combinator funding. I could not verify any YC link: ycombinator.com/companies/orgo returns 404, Orgo is absent from the published YC F26 list, and PitchBook shows ~$250K raised.

Counter-evidence to organic hype: GMGN shows 0 degen calls, 0 smart-money signals, only 14 GMGN page visits, and no paid DexScreener boosts/ads, while flagging the token as a community takeover. The official Telegram (t.me/joinOrgo) has 102 subscribers and its latest post is a "confirm humanity to access ORGO" gate. The company's own homepage makes no mention of the token.

Secondary, unverified sub-meme: a copycat token minted today named "ycomb gives them 500k btw", implying a community claim that Orgo got Y Combinator funding, which I could not substantiate anywhere.
narrative.why_spreading: The underlying sector narrative (AI agents that operate real computers) is genuine, current and reinforced by today's Opus 5.5 launch plus the OpenClaw ecosystem, and Orgo is a real shipping product with real docs and developer usage rather than a pure meme. But I found no evidence of the narrative spreading around the TOKEN today: no tweets, threads, Reddit posts, news items or call-channel chatter about $ORGO dated 2026-09-22. All indexed $ORGO social content I could retrieve is from July 2025 (Believe hackathon era) or October 2025 (a paid-DEX scanner bot). The only live, timestamped evidence of attention is on-chain: 238 unique buyers in an hour and instant copycat mints by snipers — consistent with a rotation/squeeze visible on trending scanners rather than a story propagating through social feeds.

Identity-wise the connection is real. Substantively it is much weaker: orgo.ai's homepage does not mention any token, no revenue-share, buyback or utility mechanism is documented, GMGN flags the token as a community takeover, and 50% of supply sits in a Jupiter Locker. The token is a Believe-era artifact of a startup that has since moved on, so product success does not mechanically accrue to holders.

authenticity.uncertainty: X/Twitter real-time content is effectively invisible to my tooling: direct profile fetches returned HTTP 402/403, the xcancel mirror returned 451, and search engines surfaced only 2025-era posts.
